author: Codex assessment agent /root/libertarian_historical (AI-assisted)
changeNote: Completed each of the 240 current questions as an interpreted representative doctrine, with question-specific reasoning, source references and explicit conditional neutral modelling. Separate review pending. No 12Axes answer or score imported.

metadata.name: Fascism (Italian doctrine, 1927–1932)
metadata.description: Italian Fascism as articulated around 1932: an authoritarian national state, corporatist economic coordination and expansionist politics. Historical description, not endorsement.
metadata.scope: The 1932 Mussolini/Gentile doctrine, 1927 Labour Charter and 1929 Lateran settlement, checked against historical scholarship. This specific Italian variant is not a generic label for present governments. Later 1938 racial legislation is outside scope; Nazi biological claims are not imported. Answers to later technologies are explicitly reasoned analogies from state primacy, national development and the Charter’s welfare provisions. Conditional neutrals represent questions for which state purpose overrides a fixed doctrinal rule.
metadata.phrase: An authoritarian national state that subordinates individual and class interests to national unity, corporatist coordination and expansion.

axes.brief: The doctrine rejects liberal electoral sovereignty and political competition in favour of an authoritative state claiming to embody the nation.
axes.counterEvidence: The state can consult organised interests, but its recognised syndicates do not create independent worker democracy. The rejection of numerical majority rule is explicit.

answers.rationale: The doctrine rejects government legitimacy resting on periodically counted electoral majorities.
Specialists can serve state objectives, but technical qualifications alone do not replace the authoritative national leadership.
Universal equal voting contradicts the doctrine’s repudiation of numerical political equality.
Executive authority may supersede parliamentary opposition in the claimed interest of national unity.
A plural opposition entitled to compete equally conflicts with the authoritarian one-party conception.
Independent opposition control of spending inquiries would constrain the leadership in ways the doctrine rejects.
An independent judiciary empowered to defeat supreme political decisions conflicts with comprehensive state primacy.
The Charter recognises controlled syndicates as state organs, not independent unions entitled to choose the government.
Suppressing parties regarded as threats to national unity follows the doctrine’s explicit intolerance of liberal political competition.
A binding popular repeal right would place numerical opinion above the state’s authoritative political judgement.
The leadership’s claim to embody the nation supports decisive concentrated policy authority.
Officials can be disciplined within the state, but an independent constitutional removal process constraining supreme leadership is contrary to its political structure.
Elections have no independent legitimacy capable of compelling the leadership to submit to an unwanted contest.
Popular recall would subordinate authoritative office to precisely the shifting individual opinions the doctrine rejects.
The national state is not required to derive authority from elections or independent parliamentary accountability.
Force may displace a pluralist government when represented as national regeneration, although military rule alone is not the doctrine’s institutional ideal.

axes.brief: Individual liberty is permitted insofar as the state judges it compatible with national discipline and collective purpose.
axes.counterEvidence: This does not mean the doctrine requires every conceivable surveillance measure: techniques are conditional instruments. Charter welfare protections also acknowledge regulated interests of workers.

answers.rationale: Adult private choice does not create an immunity against state regulation of drugs for discipline or national fitness.
State security authorises intrusive investigation; the proposed judicial safeguard is compatible with, but not required by, this doctrine.
An oppositional road-blocking protest would not receive an independent liberty guarantee against national-order enforcement.
Offensive criticism is not protected merely because it is nonviolent when the state treats it as subversive.
The state’s claimed comprehensive moral purpose permits paternalistic restrictions for collective strength and discipline.
Broad movement records could serve national policing, although no historical prescription for this modern technique is claimed.
Population discipline and road safety justify checks without requiring an individual suspicion-based liberty exception.
Preventive restraints can be imposed when authorities identify serious danger to the state, even before a completed offence.
Private moral choice does not override the state’s authority to control cultural expression and adult media.
Anonymous political activity has no protected priority over state identification and control of public organisation.
Threats to national order justify area-wide searches without making individual suspicion a doctrinal precondition.
Authorities may prohibit gatherings expected to undermine order or political unity.
Home privacy does not impose an absolute judicial-warrant barrier to the state’s asserted security needs.
Individual disclosure of confidential misconduct is not independently protected against the state’s disciplinary judgement.
Personal self-defence does not confer a general firearm entitlement against the state’s control of coercive force; access depends on political and public-order judgement.
Security detention is not constrained by a universal independent-court-access principle within this authoritarian conception.

axes.brief: National unity and a common public culture take priority over autonomous group identities.
axes.counterEvidence: The 1932 ethical-national conception is distinct from the later racial laws and from Nazi hereditary membership. Cultural priority here is inferred from national integration, not a fabricated genetic criterion.

answers.rationale: The doctrine treats an integrated national culture as a central object of state formation.
Accommodation may be useful pragmatically, but extra spending for separate traditions has no claim against national cultural priorities.
Residents are expected to participate in the common national ethos rather than insist on exemption from it.
Private remnants of identity may persist, but institutional loyalty to a foreign cultural community is subordinate to national integration.
A common national language serves the unified state rather than equal official standing for all migrant languages.
An Indigenous ceremony could be incorporated into national symbolism or rejected as separatist; its political meaning determines the response.
Public cultural funding would favour traditions presented as expressions of the national community.
Preserving distinct identities cannot take precedence over integration into the state’s common national purpose.
A shared public calendar reinforces national cohesion and is consistent with the Catholic settlement.
Selected traditions can be incorporated, but plural traditions do not have an equal independent claim to define national identity.
Integration is understood as incorporation into common national institutions and obligations.
Foreign-language public signage may be tolerated instrumentally, but national linguistic visibility remains privileged.
Families are expected to transmit national allegiance rather than prioritise separate inherited affiliations.
A minority religious exemption has no general priority over uniform national rules, although authorities may negotiate exceptions.
The plural coexistence of fundamentally different public ways of life conflicts with the intended ethical-national unity.
National customs and collective discipline are substantive expectations of incorporation into the community.

axes.brief: Admission is subordinate to national cohesion, manpower and state purpose rather than an individual right to migrate.
axes.counterEvidence: The selected 1932 doctrine does not prescribe one annual quota or a universal racial admission test. Conditional answers distinguish instrumental selection from later racial exclusion.

answers.rationale: The state may cap entry to protect national cohesion and capacity, though no fixed doctrinal quota is specified.
Seeking a better life does not confer an individual entitlement overriding the national state’s admission judgement.
Skills serve national strength, but ancestry, labour needs and political loyalty can also matter; an exclusively skills-based rule is too narrow.
Family reunion can support social stability, but it is permitted according to national purpose rather than an unconditional migrant right.
Humanitarian need alone cannot compel permanent admission irrespective of the state’s cultural and productive priorities.
Unlawful arrival does not establish a protected entitlement to remain against the state’s national-order decision.
Business demand remains subordinate to national planning and therefore need not overturn an admission ceiling.
Housing pressure can justify restricting immigration where the state judges domestic provision more important.
Family reunion can be limited as part of the state’s control over demographic and national integration objectives.
A job offer may demonstrate usefulness, but employers do not possess authority to determine national admission policy.
Sponsorship can serve labour discipline, while the state may admit people for other national purposes without it.
Graduation can establish useful capacity, but neither a guaranteed residence route nor an absolute exclusion follows from the doctrine.
Refugee admission can be authorised, but humanitarian status has no automatic priority over national ceilings.
Cultural compatibility assists the desired national integration, without importing a Nazi biological admission rule.
Equal immediate welfare claims by newcomers are subordinate to national membership and the state’s chosen obligations.
Cultural diversity is not an independent benefit capable of displacing the programme of national cohesion.

axes.brief: The doctrine valorises conflict, military discipline and imperial expansion, rejecting permanent peace as a supreme objective.
axes.counterEvidence: This is a doctrinal interpretation of the 1932 text, not a claim that every tactical compromise or arms agreement was impossible. Military means remain chosen by leadership.

answers.rationale: Expansion of national power can justify force without a prior attack under the doctrine’s account of imperial vitality.
Diplomacy is available, but it has no necessary priority when force better advances the national project.
Military strength warrants major sacrifices because national power is given priority over individual comfort.
An anticipated enemy threat can justify pre-emptive force without requiring the state to wait to be struck.
Restricting force to retaliation contradicts the explicit endorsement of expansion and struggle.
Compulsory male military service fits the doctrine’s emphasis on discipline, sacrifice and martial citizenship.
Concessions to avoid conflict are not preferred when they weaken prestige or the national project.
Effective autonomous weapons would be favoured by analogy with military power, qualified by their usefulness and controllability rather than individual autonomy.
Imperial ambition requires capacities beyond repelling attacks on existing national territory.
Avoiding war at any cost contradicts the text’s rejection of peace as the highest political good.
Sustained overseas campaigns are compatible with the doctrine’s endorsement of empire and expansion.
Territorial ambitions need not remain unsettled merely to preserve peace when the state judges military action advantageous.
Military threats can legitimately extract concessions in the doctrine’s power-centred international politics.
Accepting war risk to demonstrate resolve fits the doctrine’s valuation of struggle rather than giving de-escalation categorical priority.
Foreign intelligence operations serve national power even where discovery risks diplomatic conflict.
Negotiated restraint may be tactical, but reducing military capacity is not a doctrinal good when it impairs national ascendancy.

axes.brief: The state is the highest political authority; binding outside control is inconsistent with sovereign national power.
axes.counterEvidence: Treaties and alliances can be tools of expansion. Cooperation is therefore not excluded, but has no independent authority above the national state.

answers.rationale: National state authority is final rather than subordinate to international legislative institutions.
An outside body with binding authority over national policy contradicts the doctrine’s state primacy.
Domestic political-legal authority prevails when external courts would frustrate national objectives.
Alliances cannot legitimately hold final authority over the state’s chosen strategic action.
The leadership must retain freedom to abandon agreements that obstruct national power.
International judicial supremacy is incompatible with the state’s claim to final national authority.
The nation’s power and development take precedence over impartial global welfare aggregation.
Binding environmental government beyond the nation would impose an alien superior political authority.
Independent decision-making is favoured, though voluntary blocs may instrumentally advance national power.
Universal international-rights rules cannot limit the state’s asserted authority over national life.
A national currency is preferred as an instrument of sovereign economic and political direction.
Shared funds can be useful, but outside binding allocation rules have no priority over national interests.
Admission and borders belong to the sovereign national state.
Common trade rules are permissible only insofar as they serve national strategy and preserve final state discretion.
A federation transferring ultimate authority above the nation contradicts the independent imperial state ideal.
Global rules cannot demand compliance solely for universal benefit when the national state judges them disadvantageous.

axes.brief: The Labour Charter favours private initiative under state discipline and permits public intervention where private action is inadequate or political interests require it.
axes.counterEvidence: Corporatist direction is not equivalent to universal public ownership. Sector examples are applications of Charter VII–IX, which leave organisational choice conditional.

answers.rationale: Charter VII calls private initiative the most efficient normal instrument of national production, within state responsibility.
Water may require public control for national needs, but the Charter does not prescribe one ownership form for every utility.
Where outcomes are genuinely equal, the Charter’s stated preference for private initiative favours private provision.
Public firms may compete when the national interest requires intervention, without making competition itself grounds for state ownership.
The Charter’s welfare duties allow either regulated private healthcare or public provision according to national requirements.

Rail infrastructure can justify direct public ownership for strategic purposes, but Charter IX also permits control and support of private initiative. Strategic importance alone does not fix the ownership of the tracks.
Private contracting is consistent with Charter VII where cost savings preserve quality and national discipline.
Public banks may serve coordination, while regulated private banks remain compatible with the normal private-initiative principle.
Commercial assets may be transferred to private initiative, but state ownership is retained where politically useful.
Worker welfare supports housing provision without settling whether the homes must remain publicly owned.
Private defence suppliers fit the Charter where the state can effectively direct production toward military objectives.
Resource ownership is conditional on strategic control and productive adequacy rather than a universal public-property rule.
Efficient private waste provision fits the preferred ordinary private initiative when service obligations remain enforceable.
Charter IX explicitly permits intervention for political interests, supporting retention of strategically important firms.
Losses may favour transfer, but the state can retain firms for strategic or social discipline reasons.
The comprehensive ethical state has a strong reason to retain direct national broadcasting instruments, inferred rather than specified in the Charter.

axes.brief: National productive strength and independence justify trade controls, without assuming the complete later autarkic programme already existed in 1932.
axes.counterEvidence: Private enterprise and pragmatic exchange remain possible. Restrictions are instruments of national policy, not an absolute ban on commerce.

answers.rationale: Tariffs can defend production considered necessary to national strength under corporatist direction.
Unconditional barrier removal would remove instruments the state may need for economic independence.
Domestic purchases can take precedence over lower prices when they preserve national productive capacity.
Lowest global price is subordinate to national strength and the state’s strategic requirements.
Restricting dependence in essential industries follows the priority assigned to independent national power.
Unilateral liberalisation is conditional on state advantage rather than a general free-trade principle.
Temporary protection of developing industries fits state cultivation of national productive capacity.
Foreign investment has no unconditional right to equal treatment when it compromises national direction.
Agricultural protection is compatible with national provisioning and domestic productive discipline.
The state may demand industrial adjustment or protect an industry; neither response is universally required by the Charter.
Retaliatory tariffs can defend national interests and bargaining power against discriminatory foreign policy.
Equal tax treatment may be useful, but origin-based distinctions remain legitimate instruments of national economic direction.
Restricting subsidised imports can protect the state’s chosen domestic production structure.
Increasing essential dependence conflicts with the doctrine’s preference for national strength and autonomy.
Foreign strategic ownership can be restricted when it threatens effective national control, without implying a ban on all foreign capital.
Unrestricted digital exchange would be conditional on state economic and cultural control in this modern analogy.

axes.brief: Private management operates inside corporatist coordination, compulsory collective contracts and state intervention for national objectives.
axes.counterEvidence: The Charter rejects both independent class conflict and universal replacement of private initiative. It regulates wages through collective mechanisms rather than requiring one uniform numerical wage floor.

answers.rationale: Firms organise production, but Charter VII makes management responsible to the state’s national objectives.
State intervention can impose production priorities where political interests or inadequate private activity require them.
Prices may emerge commercially, but the state’s coordinating authority permits intervention against national disorganisation.
Charter VI and IX permit coordination and intervention to steer investment toward national production goals.
Consumer demand cannot override corporatist national production priorities simply by reflecting private preference.
Essential-price regulation is compatible with state intervention to protect national provisioning and labour stability.
Entry can be conditioned on the state’s corporatist organisation of production rather than protected as an unconditional private right.
Credit may be directed where necessary for nationally coordinated industrial activity.
Capital movement is subordinate to national economic purpose rather than independent owner discretion alone.
Sector subsidies can advance productive priorities within the Charter’s intervention framework.
Independent currencies escaping national coordination conflict with the political unity of the state-directed economy.
Charter XII requires collective wages to consider living needs and productivity, but does not prescribe a universal statutory minimum.

Charter XII entrusts wage determination to collective agreements between employer and worker organisations, within compulsory state supervision and national-production constraints, rather than prescribing one government wage schedule.
Monetary institutions can support the state’s integrated national economic objectives.
Market rents may coexist with intervention when worker welfare or national interest requires it.
Corporatist organs coordinate ordinary production, while private managers retain operational responsibility.

axes.brief: The Charter promises social insurance and worker protection while rejecting egalitarian class politics and preserving productive hierarchy.
axes.counterEvidence: Collective wage provisions and maternity, accident and old-age assistance are substantive commitments. They are neither universal income equality nor merely charity.

answers.rationale: Income differences alone are not a target when hierarchy and productive incentives serve the national community.
The doctrine rejects egalitarian class levelling, while allowing intervention against conditions that damage national cohesion.
A stronger income floor can serve worker welfare, but national production and fiscal priorities determine whether higher taxes for it are justified.

The Charter supports social insurance beyond destitution, but does not make substantially narrowing differences in living standards its goal. Its occupational welfare model does not fit either side of this basic-safety-net versus income-gap contrast without qualification.
Progressive tax rates can be adopted for state purposes, while preserving hierarchy prevents a categorical egalitarian commitment.
Private productive rewards are accepted despite inequality, subject to obligations toward the national state.
Inheritance can support continuity, but state fiscal demands can justify taxation; no fixed inheritance-tax doctrine follows.
Work discipline supports conditions on assistance, while social insurance supports continuing protection; a universal time limit is not prescribed.
Taxing wealth is permissible for national purposes but reducing wealth as such is not the Charter’s governing objective.
The state balances revenue, production and social insurance rather than necessarily choosing low taxes and modest benefits.
Organised worker welfare and education extend beyond survival toward participation in the national community.
Tax cuts are justified when productive priorities favour them, but cannot automatically displace corporatist welfare commitments.
Securing adequate worker livelihoods is compatible with supplementary support where wages fail national welfare requirements.
A flat marginal tax structure has no special authority within a doctrine that judges taxation by national function.
Land redistribution may serve national production, while private initiative and hierarchy may favour existing holdings; compensation alone does not decide.

Social insurance can cover workers beyond destitution, while work discipline and productive hierarchy constrain assistance. Educational and maternity services alone do not establish a general rule extending cash benefits to all low-income households.

axes.brief: The Lateran settlement gives Catholicism official public standing while preserving the Fascist state’s political supremacy.
axes.counterEvidence: Religious establishment is not unrestricted government by clergy. Church-state accommodation and independent clerical legislative veto are different propositions.

answers.rationale: The Catholic settlement gives religious commitments a public legal role, inconsistent with excluding all religious influence from law.
Religious principles inform family and education law through the Concordat without becoming the sole source of state authority.
The political state does not require a general clerical permission for every law under the Lateran settlement.
Treaty Article 1 confirms Catholicism’s official status in the Italian state.
The Concordat gives Catholic religious teaching a privileged role rather than a wholly neutral public-school framework.
The settlement supports Catholic instruction in public education.
Ordinary state courts coexist with ecclesiastical matrimonial jurisdiction, so neither exclusive civil nor universal religious adjudication describes the arrangement.

The Lateran settlement gives the Church a negotiated role in specified religious and educational arrangements, while the Fascist state retains political authority. This supports limited consultation without a general clerical review requirement for proposed laws.
Official religious observance fits the Catholic establishment, though worship is not the entire source of political legitimacy.
The settlement’s recognition of church institutions supports public assistance rather than strict separation of financial relations.
Catholic symbolism is consistent with the established religious settlement and need not be removed from public institutions.
Recognising religious holidays in the public calendar is consistent with the Catholic establishment.
Clerical office alone does not confer a general automatic right to political office under the state-centred doctrine.
The Concordat protects specified ecclesiastical revenues and abolishes special church-property taxes, supporting privileged fiscal treatment beyond general charitable equivalence.
Concordat recognition of Catholic marriage conflicts with abolishing every religious legal role in marital validity.
The settlement recognises ecclesiastical authority over specified matrimonial matters rather than insisting on exclusively civil family jurisdiction.

axes.brief: Family continuity and religious public morality coexist with a revolutionary project to reshape national character.
axes.counterEvidence: The 1932 doctrine is not simple preservation of every inherited institution: it rejects liberal precedents and insists the state can transform citizens. Modern identity questions are conditional institutional analogies.

answers.rationale: Inherited customs can be transformed for the national project, but individual lifestyle preference does not itself justify change.
The Catholic family settlement and national continuity support established traditions when compatible with state objectives.
Official recognition of established marriage gives some family forms priority rather than an equal claim for every arrangement.
The Charter’s distinct maternity protections and Catholic family framework support differentiated roles without implying women never work.
The Catholic matrimonial settlement does not support legal recognition of same-sex marriage.
Established marital family life is privileged as a source of social continuity and national formation.
Individual social preference is insufficient to override the public moral and family obligations of the selected settlement.
Family religious authority matters, but parents cannot hold an absolute veto over the state’s national educational mission.
The established marriage framework favours conventional family placement rather than an equal claim for same-sex couples.
An ethical state with recognised religious morality can prescribe public modesty rather than leaving it entirely to personal choice.
Identity-based language reform has no inherent priority over the state’s established moral and cultural categories.
Public moral continuity is generally preferred to unrestricted experimentation, unless the state’s own project requires transformation.
Productive mobilisation can permit unconventional roles, while family ideals impose limits; no universal acceptance or prohibition follows.
The doctrine values continuity but also revolutionary state action, so gradualism is not a necessary method of institutional change.
The state may teach about sexual difference for its own moral purposes; descriptive instruction does not necessarily imply equal approval of every identity.
Ancestral custom can express national continuity, but the state may discard it when it obstructs its transformative purpose.

axes.brief: National productive and military development can justify rapid innovation, but the doctrine does not specify modern clinical or ecological thresholds.
axes.counterEvidence: The Charter includes health protection, so enthusiasm for technology does not establish opposition to all safety trials. Technology answers are explicit conditional analogies rather than historical policy quotations.

answers.rationale: New technology useful to national strength would generally receive support without treating every uncertainty as a reason to prohibit it.
Trials can protect productive health, while urgent national usefulness can justify earlier deployment; no universal waiting threshold follows.
Infrastructure serving national production can outweigh habitat preservation where state priorities require expansion.
Medical benefit and worker protection both matter; the doctrine does not specify how much long-term evidence is always sufficient.
Productivity-enhancing AI fits national development, although corporatist management may address displaced labour.
Habitat protection has no general priority over national construction and productive power in the selected doctrine.
Cultivated meat could aid provisioning, but health and state usefulness determine acceptance rather than novelty alone.
Controlled trials can serve national health, but the doctrine establishes no categorical restriction of every brain implant to trials.
Technological capacity fits the emphasis on national production more readily than treating reduced consumption as the preferred universal response.
Uncertainty may justify investigation, but national development can warrant proceeding; the balance depends on the project’s importance.
Basic adult consent and safety do not settle state approval, which also turns on national usefulness and social discipline.
Reliability testing of medical AI supports the Charter’s worker-health responsibilities where errors would impair health and productive capacity.
Hereditary enhancement is not specified by this 1932 ethical-state doctrine; neither Nazi eugenics nor unrestricted individual choice is imported.
Agricultural output and public health both matter, leaving the duration of GMO testing contingent on the assessed national consequences.
Housing construction meeting national social needs can take priority over retaining undeveloped land.
Possible irreversible harm is relevant to national welfare but does not create a categorical veto against state-selected development.

axes.brief: The unified state takes precedence over autonomous regional authority.
axes.counterEvidence: Corporatist and local administration can perform delegated functions. Administrative decentralisation does not create a right to resist national political decisions.

answers.rationale: Protected regional power against the national state conflicts with comprehensive political unity.
Final authority in territorial disputes belongs to the national state rather than independently sovereign regions.
A regional majority cannot dissolve national unity through a unilateral secession vote.
National authorities can override regional programmes when they conflict with the integrated national project.
Independent regional constitutions would subordinate state unity to separate territorial authority.
National policing supports uniform political discipline and control across the territory.
Regional retention of revenue is subordinate to the state’s national allocation and development priorities.
A common national curriculum serves the ethical state’s formation of citizens.
Local tax variation may be administratively useful, but it has no protected priority against national economic coordination.
The Labour Charter’s national corporatist system supports nationwide employment organisation and standards.
Local boundary changes cannot bypass the national state’s authority over its territorial organisation.
Worker-health obligations can be coordinated nationally rather than dependent solely on local discretion.
Separate Indigenous political sovereignty conflicts with the doctrine’s unitary national authority.
National coordination can restrict local tax competition when it impairs integrated economic policy.
Local conservation choices are subordinate to national development and political objectives.
National mobilisation in disasters follows the priority given to a coordinated and capable state.

axes.brief: The 1932 doctrine stresses ethical formation, discipline and the remaking of national character rather than a comprehensive genetic explanation of behaviour.
axes.counterEvidence: This does not establish empirical social causation for every trait. Neutral answers reflect a spiritual-voluntarist doctrine outside the questions’ simple biological-versus-social contrast; later racial legislation is excluded.

answers.rationale: The state’s formative mission assumes upbringing and discipline substantially reshape citizens’ conduct.
This selected text does not establish inherited national intelligence as a primary cause; its spiritual-national account is not a measured IQ theory.
Traditional roles coexist with state-directed formation, leaving the relative biological and social causes of sex differences undetermined.
Martial discipline addresses fear, but it does not specify whether stress differences are mainly inherited or learned.
National education and organised work presume experience can develop interests and capacities.
Celebrating courage does not entail a claim that risk-taking differences are primarily inherited.
Corporatist organisation and ethical education are intended to cultivate cooperation across social classes.
Subordinating private sympathy to duty is normative and does not establish biological primacy for empathy variation.
Discipline can train attention, but the doctrine supplies no predominance rule comparing training with neurobiological differences.
Its spiritual account of ethical duty is not reducible to a primarily biological explanation of moral attitudes.
National narratives shape perceived enemies, but this does not settle the overall causal balance in human threat responses.
Character formation is stressed without specifying a general empirical heritability estimate for temperament.
The ethical-state doctrine does not rank cultural influence and inherited tendencies as explanations of preferences about physical attractiveness.
The 1932 ethical-state account is not coded as the later Nazi-style hereditary racial theory of violence.
The emphasis on training, education and discipline favours cultivable self-control rather than a fixed racial determination.
The Charter uses productivity and collective wage institutions together, so it does not reduce pay differences solely to economic value or social expectations.

review.reviewer: Codex /root, separate evidence review of /root/libertarian_historical assessment
review.notes: Read all 240 answers against their exact wording, with the 1932 doctrine, 1927 Labour Charter, 1929 Lateran Treaty/Concordat and USHMM historical account. Preserved the 1927–1932 scope rather than importing 1938 racial legislation. Corrected the collective wage-negotiation answer: state-supervised bargaining is still bargaining and is not identical to a government wage schedule. Distinguished cash-benefit targeting from broader services, rail infrastructure ownership from operation, and a religious consultative role from a legislative veto. Neutral answers retain explicit conditional judgements under state primacy or a non-ranking ethical conception; modern technology answers are labelled analogies. No answer changed to target scores or reduce similarity.
